solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: He who's conceited concealing desire to arrive

indicators.note: to conceal something is to hide it inside, so one word wraps round the other

parts.note: a pup is a conceited young man
an itch is a restless desire

explanation.surface: A vain young man hides his longing to turn up.
explanation.walkthrough: Chambers gives pup as a conceited young fellow, a sense few solvers know; desire is a restless craving here.
explanation.definitionFit: To pitch up is an informal phrasal verb for turning up somewhere.

clue.text: Humiliated and laid in lavender, afternoon is wasted

indicators.note: something wasted is lost, so it disappears from the word

parts.note: to lay in lavender is an old idiom for pawning goods
a is an abbreviation for afternoon

explanation.surface: A wasted afternoon spent lying in lavender left someone feeling foolish.
explanation.walkthrough: PWNED is gamers' slang, born of a typo for owned, meaning thoroughly beaten.
explanation.definitionFit: In online gaming slang, to be pwned is to be crushingly defeated and humbled.

clue.text: Brass, an early Persian bit

parts.note: brass and tom are both slang for a prostitute
taken as written

explanation.surface: A brass coin used in old Persia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brass' looks like the metal of the coin, but it is rhyming slang (brass nail) for a prostitute, as is tom.
explanation.definitionFit: A toman was a former Persian gold coin, and bit is slang for a coin.

clue.text: Miss is in court being incomparably careful

indicators.note: one thing in another is placed inside it

parts.note: CT is the abbreviation for court
to miss something is to lose it
the contracted 's, as in it's

explanation.surface: A young woman in court is being extremely cautious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miss' looks like a young lady but is the verb, and 'is' shrinks to the contracted 's.
explanation.definitionFit: Close can mean secretive or guarded, so closest is the most guarded, beyond comparison.

clue.text: Lamp-lighting lover, an illustrious person

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the priestess of Greek myth who lit a lamp to guide her swimming lover Leander
second meaning: someone admired for great deeds

explanation.walkthrough: The mythical Hero lit a lamp each night so Leander could swim the Hellespont to her.
explanation.definitionFit: A hero is a person celebrated for courage or achievement, while Hero is also the name of the lamp-lighting priestess.

clue.text: A concupiscence runs through mate coming from The Marshes?

indicators.note: running through something means passing inside it

parts.note: a pal is a mate or friend
taken as written
concupiscence is sexual desire
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Desire runs through a partner who hails from marshy country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runs' looks like the container signal on its own, but it also supplies R; through does the placing.
explanation.definitionFit: Palustral is from Latin palus, a marsh, so it describes things of the marshes.

clue.text: She who adventured despite no longer wanting money

indicators.note: no longer wanting something means doing without it, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: despite in its old sense is spite or malice
M is the abbreviation for money

explanation.surface: A woman went on adventures even though she was no longer short of cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Despite' looks like a preposition but is the noun meaning spite; drop M from MALICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Alice is the heroine of Lewis Carroll's Alice's Adventures in Wonderland.

clue.text: At most in Naples a Latin pulled up round one

parts.note: taken as written
L is the abbreviation for Latin

indicators.note: pulled up in a down clue means drawn upward, so the letters run bottom to top
going round something means surrounding it

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: In Naples, a Latin speaker at most pulls up around one o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: The word 'up' in 'pulled up' does double work, being both the letters turned and part of the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Al più is the Italian phrase for at most, used as a musical direction.

clue.text: Lifting cold coffee — gods, perfect

indicators.note: lifting in a down clue raises the letters, so they read bottom to top

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
Illy is an Italian coffee brand
di is Latin for gods

explanation.surface: Raising a glass of iced coffee, the gods call it heavenly.
explanation.definitionFit: Idyllic describes a scene of ideal, untroubled happiness.

clue.text: Climax follows this as cast is at high

indicators.note: someone high is intoxicated, and so are the letters, which lurch out of order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The play's climax comes next while the actors are flying high.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface of a cast on stage ties the wordplay to the drama term.
explanation.definitionFit: In classical drama the catastasis is the part where action heightens just before the climax.

clue.text: Dissatisfied six caught by English common sense

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for English

indicators.note: something caught by another is held within it

parts.note: nous is practical common sense
VI is the Roman numeral six

explanation.surface: Six people are unhappy at English pragmatism.
explanation.definitionFit: Being envious means resentful of what others have, so discontented with one's lot.

clue.text: What sets Arfur off? Being into dodgy old wheels flogged to trade

indicators.note: something dodgy is unreliable and crooked, so these letters are not to be trusted in their order
what sets something off is what starts it, so only its opening letter is wanted

parts.note: the opening letter of Arfur
taken as written

explanation.surface: Arthur Daley, the cockney wheeler-dealer of TV's Minder, flogging dodgy second-hand cars.
explanation.walkthrough: Arfur is Arthur Daley, the shady car dealer of the British TV series Minder; his A goes into the mix with OLD WHEELS.
explanation.definitionFit: To wholesale goods is to sell them in bulk to the trade rather than to the public.

clue.text: Half skipping next practical lesson about woodlands

indicators.note: skipping half of a word means leaving out half its letters

parts.note: taken as written
the moral of a story is the practical lesson it teaches

explanation.surface: A teacher skips half the next hands-on lesson on forests.
explanation.definitionFit: Nemoral is an adjective meaning of or inhabiting woods or groves.

clue.text: Big enough to read elegy and believe all but two changes

indicators.note: something that changes takes a new form, so the letters are rearranged
all but two means every letter save the final pair

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An elegy printed large enough to read is hard to credit.
explanation.definitionFit: Eye-legible text is large enough to be read by the naked eye without magnification.

clue.text: Dire subscription service here could be seen as depravity

indicators.note: what could be seen as another word is a rearrangement of it

parts.note: taken as written, the part supplied in the clue
the whole that the two parts rearrange to

explanation.surface: A grumble that a dreadful TV subscription channel is morally corrupt.
explanation.walkthrough: A compound anagram: DIRE plus the answer rearranges to DEPRAVITY, so take DIRE's letters away from DEPRAVITY and what remains is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Pay TV is television bought by subscription rather than free to air.

clue.text: Tree's roll of curled bark, a first sign of illness

parts.note: a quill is a roll of dried bark, as with cinnamon
taken as written

indicators.note: the first sign of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letter of illness

explanation.surface: A tree's peeling bark curls up, an early symptom of disease.
explanation.definitionFit: Quillai is the Chilean soapbark tree, whose bark yields saponin.

clue.text: Shut up quarterly that is bygone grief (close to Duke)

parts.note: qu. is an abbreviation for quarterly
i.e. is short for id est, that is
tene is an archaic word for grief
D is the abbreviation for duke

explanation.surface: A quarterly journal silences long-past sorrow, near to a duke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close to' just places D beside the grief, not taking the last letter of Duke.
explanation.definitionFit: Quietened is the past tense of a verb meaning to make silent, which is what shut up means.

clue.text: Reduction with extra eccentricity to retail freely

indicators.note: taking something extra on board means admitting it within

parts.note: a dent is a reduction, as in a dent in savings
e is the mathematical symbol for the eccentricity of a conic

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper slashes prices and adds quirks to sell goods freely.
explanation.walkthrough: E goes inside DENT. 'Eccentricity' seems to mean oddness, but here it is the symbol from conic geometry.
explanation.definitionFit: To denet goods was to free them from the Net Book Agreement so retailers could set their own prices.

clue.text: Blocking prodigal son too

indicators.note: what is blocking a passage sits within it, so the answer lies inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the gap between the two words

explanation.surface: The returning prodigal son gets in the way as well.
explanation.definitionFit: Also and too are synonyms, both meaning in addition.

clue.text: Lingual problem — a tendency to comment comically, we may think

definitions.meaning: first meaning: inflammation of the tongue

definitions.text: a tendency to comment comically, we may think
definitions.meaning: second meaning: read jokingly as a compulsive habit of glossing, with -itis as the joke suffix for a craze

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the word into GLOSS, to comment, and the jokey suffix -itis used for any obsessive habit; 'we may think' flags it as whimsical.
explanation.definitionFit: Glossitis is the medical term for an inflamed tongue, the tongue being the organ of speech.

clue.text: Greek goddess in part of play rubbed rock, say

parts.note: Ge is the Greek earth goddess, also called Gaia
in and of can be interchangeable, as in a man in his prime or of his time
an act is a division of a play

explanation.surface: A Greek goddess appears in a scene of a play, worn down like stone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a placing signal, but it supplies OF.
explanation.definitionFit: A geofact is a stone shaped by natural wear, such as rubbing, that looks man-made, so a rubbed rock is an example.

clue.text: Expand on dock forcibly

parts.note: O is an abbreviation for on
a pen is a dock for submarines
out can mean by force, as in throw out

explanation.surface: Swelling crowds burst onto the dock by force.
explanation.definitionFit: To open out is a phrasal verb for spreading or becoming wider, a synonym of expand.

clue.text: Manoeuvre retakes male bird of prey

indicators.note: to manoeuvre is to move things around into a new position

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A falcon swoops again to snatch its prey.
explanation.definitionFit: A sakeret is the male of the saker, a large falcon used in falconry.

clue.text: Raise chat about what people bitten by, say, spiders should get

definitions.text: what people bitten by, say, spiders should get

indicators.note: turned about suggests letters moved around into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Bring up in conversation the treatment for spider bites.
explanation.definitionFit: A theriac is an old remedy against venomous bites, so a bitten person needs theriacas.

clue.text: Fancy moulding of Trump's suit

parts.note: o' is a shortened form of of, as in o'clock
to gee is to suit or get along with someone; the name is surface dressing

explanation.surface: The ornate trim on Donald Trump's suit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trump's suit' sends you to clothes or card suits, but the useful word is the verb suit, meaning get on with.
explanation.definitionFit: An ogee is an S-shaped curve used as a decorative moulding in architecture.

clue.text: Sri Lankan verse collection of ancient tales

parts.note: V is the abbreviation for verse
the Edda is a collection of Old Norse myths and sagas

explanation.surface: A Sri Lankan book of verse and old legends.
explanation.definitionFit: The Vedda are the aboriginal people of Sri Lanka, so a Vedda is a Sri Lankan native.

clue.text: King before opening to habitually exercise arbitrary decree

indicators.note: a word opening up to admit others lets them in between its letters

parts.note: to use something is to exercise it habitually
K is the chess abbreviation for king
A stands for ante, Latin for before

explanation.surface: A ruler who routinely issues capricious edicts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Before' looks like a positional instruction, but it supplies A, from ante as in a.m.
explanation.definitionFit: A ukase was an edict of the Russian tsar, hence any high-handed order.

clue.text: Ring up a new date

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the letters climb, reading bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new
an era is a date from which time is counted

explanation.surface: Phone someone to arrange a new appointment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring up' reads as phoning, but Ring is the definition and up turns the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: An arena is a ring or enclosed space where contests are held, as a boxing ring is.

clue.text: Worried, starting off on the losing side?

indicators.note: with its start off, a word loses its opening letter

parts.note: the losing side has been beaten

explanation.surface: Anxious from the very start about being on the team that loses.
explanation.definitionFit: Eaten as in eaten up means consumed by anxiety, so troubled or worried.

clue.text: Something which stabilises grass sheltered from the east

parts.note: to grass is to inform, and a fink is an informer

indicators.note: read from the east means read from right to left in an across clue

parts.note: the lee is the sheltered side

explanation.surface: A lawn is protected from easterly winds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grass' is not a lawn but British slang for an informer, as is the American fink.
explanation.definitionFit: A fin keel is a deep narrow keel fixed under a yacht to keep it steady.

clue.text: Black behind deep sea fish

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black on pencils
ass is slang for the behind or backside

explanation.surface: A dark fish lurks behind in the ocean depths.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Behind' looks like a position word but it is the noun for the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: The bass is a sea fish, and the word also means deep in pitch, so the definition covers both.

clue.text: A drummer died, going west, poetically astray

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: going west in an across clue means travelling leftward, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: DR is the abbreviation for drummer
ob. is short for obiit, Latin for died

explanation.surface: A drummer dies, going west in the old sense, and loses his way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going west' also means dying, which fits the surface, but it is the turnaround signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Abord is an old literary adverb for off course or astray, found in poetry.

clue.text: Superlatively stingy are in cosy pad

indicators.note: one thing in another is placed within it

parts.note: a nest is a snug home
taken as written

explanation.surface: The meanest people live in comfortable flats.
explanation.definitionFit: Near is an old word for stingy, so the superlative nearest means most miserly.

clue.text: In another way nurse needs instinctive grasp?

indicators.note: putting things another way means presenting them differently, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A nurse needs a gut feeling for patients, put differently.
explanation.definitionFit: An undersense is a deeper or underlying awareness, a feeling below conscious thought.

clue.text: Poetic plant, mostly Anacreontic, translator picked up

indicators.note: something picked up is taken in and held
mostly means all but a little, so the last letter goes

parts.note: Anacreon came from Teos, so Tean is an adjective for him
TR is the abbreviation for translator

explanation.surface: A translator renders a poem about a plant in the style of Anacreon.
explanation.walkthrough: Anacreon, the Greek lyric poet, was born in Teos, so Tean means of Teos; cut to TEA, it holds TR.
explanation.definitionFit: Tetra is an old literary word for a plant, found only in poetry, hence poetic.

clue.text: Sully infernal place west of Highland royal burgh

parts.note: Dis is the underworld or Hell
Tain is a small royal burgh in the Scottish Highlands

explanation.surface: A Highland town lies to the west of Hell, a stain on its name.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue, west of means placed before.
explanation.definitionFit: Distain is an old verb meaning to stain or dishonour.
